title: Chain-level supertrace computation, with explicit conventions
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $P^\bullet=(P^i,d^i)$ be a bounded cochain complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $P^i=0$ outside a finite interval, and $d^{i+1}d^i=0$. Let $v:P^\bullet\to P^\bullet$ be a chain map of degree zero. Work in the usual symmetric monoidal category of these complexes, with total tensor differential and Koszul symmetry
$$d(p\otimes q)=dp\otimes q+(-1)^{|p|}p\otimes dq,\qquad c(p\otimes q)=(-1)^{|p||q|}q\otimes p,$$
unit $A[0]$, and the canonical tensor associators and unit isomorphisms (suppressed in the formulas). These are the total tensor conventions of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to ordinary modules on the category with one object and only its identity morphism, with only the maximal sieve covering.

Put $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,A[0])$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], explicitly
$$ (P^\vee)^j=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-j},A),\qquad (d^\vee\varphi)(x)=(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(dx). $$
For each $i$ choose a finite dual frame $(e_{i,a},\epsilon_{i,a})_a$ of $P^i$, meaning $e_{i,a}\in P^i$, $\epsilon_{i,a}:P^i\to A$ linear, and $x=\sum_a e_{i,a}\epsilon_{i,a}(x)$. Choose the empty frame when $P^i=0$, and place $\epsilon_{i,a}$ in degree $-i$. Define
$$\operatorname{ev}_P(\varphi\otimes p)=\varphi(p)\quad\text{if }|\varphi|+|p|=0,$$
with evaluation zero on other total degrees, and
$$\operatorname{coev}_P(1)=\sum_{i,a}e_{i,a}\otimes\epsilon_{i,a}.$$
For a finitely generated projective module $M$ with finite dual frame $(e_a,\epsilon_a)$, write $\operatorname{Tr}_A(t\mid M)=\sum_a\epsilon_a(t e_a)$ for its ordinary projective-module trace; it is independent of the frame and agrees with the usual diagonal matrix sum when $M$ is finite free. This specifies the meaning of ordinary trace here even when $M$ has no basis.

Then:

(a) These formulas give well-defined, frame-independent degree-zero chain maps $\operatorname{ev}_P:P^\vee\otimes P\to A[0]$ and $\operatorname{coev}_P:A[0]\to P\otimes P^\vee$.

(b) With the canonical associators and unit maps inserted, the triangle identities hold:
$$ (\operatorname{ev}_P\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\operatorname{coev}_P)=1_{P^\vee},\qquad (1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_P)\circ(\operatorname{coev}_P\otimes1)=1_P. $$

(c) The categorical trace of [sk-d-trace], namely $\operatorname{ev}_P\circ c_{P,P^\vee}\circ(v\otimes1)\circ\operatorname{coev}_P$, is multiplication by
$$ \operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}_A(v^i\mid P^i)\in A. $$
In particular its value on $1_P$ is the Euler characteristic scalar $\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{rk}_A(P^i)$, where the projective rank scalar means $\operatorname{rk}_A(M):=\operatorname{Tr}_A(1_M\mid M)\in A$, not an assumed constant integer rank. For a finite free term of rank $r_i$ this scalar is $r_i\cdot1_A$.

The same formulas compute the categorical trace in the derived category $D(A)$ of ordinary $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$, on the perfect object represented by $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. They are invariant under chain homotopy, and under replacing a perfect representative and its endomorphism by an isomorphic pair in $D(A)$. Thus they define a function $\operatorname{tr}_A:\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(Q(P))\to A$. When $A=A_{E,n}$ with the finite-coefficient datum of [def-trf-categorical-trace], this is exactly the trace defined there, including its transported duality maps and scalar identification.

proof.text: Finite dual frames exist without assuming freeness. Choose a finite generating family of a term $M$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; it gives a surjection $\pi:A^N\to M$. Apply the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to $1_M$ to obtain $\iota:M\to A^N$ with $\pi\iota=1_M$. For the standard coordinate vectors $u_a$, set $e_a=\pi(u_a)$ and $\epsilon_a=\operatorname{pr}_a\iota$. Then $\sum_a e_a\epsilon_a(x)=\pi\iota(x)=x$. Use $N=0$ for zero terms. The dual module has inclusion $\pi^*:M^*\to(A^N)^*$ and retraction $\iota^*$, whose composite is $(\pi\iota)^*=1$, so it is a direct summand of $(A^N)^*\cong A^N$. For a second splitting $L\xrightarrow{j}A^T\xrightarrow{q}L$, the tensor inclusion $\iota\otimes j$ and retraction $\pi\otimes q$ compose to $1_{M\otimes L}$ in $A^N\otimes A^T\cong A^{NT}$. The dual and tensor are projective by the cited direct-summand characterization, and finite because the retractions send finitely many coordinate vectors to generators. A finite direct sum of these retracts is a retract of the finite direct sum of their finite free modules, using the block-diagonal inclusions and retractions. Thus duals and the finite total tensors stay in the stated category. This is the explicit two-line splitting argument of Stacks Tag 00NX, algebra.tex, lemma-finite-projective, (2) implies (3), using the cited definitions rather than invoking an extra theorem.

source.place: Opening and unit proof: choose finite dual frames by splitting a finite free module; Stacks Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective, (2) implies (3)

proof.text: The coevaluation tensor is independent of frames. For any two frames $(e_a,\epsilon_a)$ and $(q_b,\mu_b)$ of $M$, the frame identities give $e_a=\sum_b q_b\mu_b(e_a)$ and $\mu_b=\sum_a\mu_b(e_a)\epsilon_a$. Bilinearity therefore gives $\sum_a e_a\otimes\epsilon_a=\sum_b q_b\otimes\mu_b$. Apply this degreewise; boundedness and the empty frames on zero terms make the total sum finite. This argument also proves independence of the splitting in step 1.

source.place: Step 5, independence of the chosen bases, corrected to finite dual frames

proof.text:
The projective trace and its cyclicity follow by finite expansion, with no free-module trace theorem required. For frames $(e_a,\epsilon_a)$ on $M$ and $(q_b,\mu_b)$ on $N$ and maps $f:M\to N$, $g:N\to M$, expand $f(e_a)$ in the second frame to get
$$\sum_a\epsilon_a(gf(e_a))=\sum_{a,b}\mu_b(f(e_a))\epsilon_a(g(q_b))=\sum_b\mu_b(fg(q_b)).$$
For $N=M$, $f=t$, $g=1$, and two choices of frame, this proves frame independence of $\operatorname{Tr}_A(t)$. For arbitrary $M,N$ it gives $\operatorname{Tr}_M(gf)=\operatorname{Tr}_N(fg)$. Linearity follows from the finite-sum formula. With a genuine basis and its coordinate functionals the formula is precisely the diagonal matrix sum; in particular the identity on $A^r$ has trace $r\cdot1_A$.

source.place: Step 4, ordinary trace interpretation; Step 5, cyclicity used for homotopy invariance

proof.text: The signed conventions actually give complexes and chain maps for the symmetry. The dual differential is the differential of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] with target $A[0]$; explicitly $(d^\vee)^2\varphi(x)=(-1)^{j+2}(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(d^2x)=0$. For the total tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the mixed terms of $d^2(p\otimes q)$ have signs $(-1)^{i+1}$ and $(-1)^i$ and cancel. If $|p|=i,|q|=j$, both $cd(p\otimes q)$ and $dc(p\otimes q)$ equal $(-1)^{ij}dq\otimes p+(-1)^{ij+j}q\otimes dp$, so the symmetry is a chain map. Its square is $1$. The canonical reassociation map sends $(p\otimes q)\otimes r$ to $p\otimes(q\otimes r)$; in either parenthesization its three differential terms have coefficients $1,(-1)^i,(-1)^{i+j}$. The unit maps send $a\otimes p$ and $p\otimes a$ to $ap$ and commute with the differential since $a$ has degree zero. Both pentagon paths send a fourfold pure tensor to the same final parenthesization; the unit triangle sends $(p\otimes a)\otimes q$ to $p\otimes aq=ap\otimes q$. The hexagon sign equality is $(-1)^{i(j+k)}=(-1)^{ij}(-1)^{ik}$. These checks extend from pure tensors by linearity. For degree-zero maps $f,g$, the two sides of $c(f\otimes g)=(g\otimes f)c$ send $p\otimes q$ to $(-1)^{ij}g(q)\otimes f(p)$, proving the naturality used below. Thus suppressing these canonical maps is legitimate, without claiming that tensor parentheses are literal equalities.

source.place: Explicit conventions and Step 1, square of the dual differential

proof.text:
Evaluation has degree zero by its stated zero extension. Its chain-map identity only needs checking on input of total degree $-1$, since only there can evaluation of its differential be nonzero. For $\varphi\in(P^\vee)^j$ and $p\in P^{-j-1}$, it is
$$\operatorname{ev}(d(\varphi\otimes p))=(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(dp)+(-1)^j\varphi(dp)=0.$$
In every other input degree both sides vanish by degree. The target $A[0]$ has zero differential, proving (a) for evaluation.

source.place: Step 1, evaluation is a degree-zero chain map

proof.text:
Coevaluation is closed, by cancellation with the actual frames. In the summand $P^{i+1}\otimes(P^i)^*$, the differential of its value at $1$ is
$$\sum_a d^ie_{i,a}\otimes\epsilon_{i,a}-\sum_b e_{i+1,b}\otimes(\epsilon_{i+1,b}\circ d^i).$$
Indeed the sign in the second part is $(-1)^{i+1}(-1)^{-(i+1)+1}=-1$. Expand $d^ie_{i,a}=\sum_b e_{i+1,b}\epsilon_{i+1,b}(d^ie_{i,a})$ and $\epsilon_{i+1,b}\circ d^i=\sum_a\epsilon_{i+1,b}(d^ie_{i,a})\epsilon_{i,a}$. These are identical finite double sums with opposite signs. This proves the degree-zero coevaluation is a chain map, completing (a).

source.place: Step 2, coevaluation is a chain map, with corrected dual-frame indices

proof.text: For $p\in P^i$, the second triangle composite is $\sum_a e_{i,a}\epsilon_{i,a}(p)=p$. For $\psi\in(P^i)^*$, the first is $\sum_a\psi(e_{i,a})\epsilon_{i,a}=\psi$, as follows by applying $\psi$ to the frame identity for each $x\in P^i$. Evaluation annihilates every other degree. Canonical associators and unit maps only reparenthesize these tensors, so this proves both triangle identities (b). No symmetry is used in these two composites.

Use exactly the trace composite in [sk-d-trace]. On $1$ its successive values are $\sum_{i,a}e_{i,a}\otimes\epsilon_{i,a}$, then $\sum_{i,a}v^ie_{i,a}\otimes\epsilon_{i,a}$, then $\sum_{i,a}(-1)^{i(-i)}\epsilon_{i,a}\otimes v^ie_{i,a}$, and finally $\sum_{i,a}(-1)^i\epsilon_{i,a}(v^ie_{i,a})$. Here $v$ has degree zero and $-i^2\equiv i\pmod2$, including negative $i$. By the trace definition and step 3 this is the asserted alternating sum of ordinary projective traces. For $v=1$, it is the stated Euler characteristic scalar, with the usual $r_i\cdot1_A$ interpretation for a free term. This proves (c).

source.place: Step 4, trace of the composite; unit proof, the dual factor has degree -i

proof.text:
If $v-v'=ds+sd$ with $s^i:P^i\to P^{i-1}$, linearity and the rectangular cyclicity proved in step 3 give
$$\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}_{P^i}(d^{i-1}s^i)+\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}_{P^i}(s^{i+1}d^i)
=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}_{P^{i-1}}(s^id^{i-1})+\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}_{P^j}(s^{j+1}d^j)=0,$$
where in the first sum put $j=i-1$. All sums are finite. Thus the scalar descends to homotopy classes, rather than simply identifying homotopy classes with derived morphisms without justification.

source.place: Step 5, invariance under homotopy, with the index shift written out

proof.text: The chain tensor calculation computes the derived tensor calculation. Every term of $P$ and $P^\vee$ is projective by step 1, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. They are bounded above, so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes both complexes K-flat. Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with the identity map $A\to A$: the identity K-flat resolutions compute all tensor products of these representatives and their morphisms in $D(A)$. Consequently the evaluation, coevaluation and Koszul symmetry just checked represent their derived maps. For the unit scalar use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]: $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A[0])\cong\operatorname{End}_A(A)\cong A$, the last map sending $h$ to $h(1)$ with inverse multiplication by that scalar. Thus the scalar computed in step 8 is also the derived categorical trace.

source.place: Opening paragraph, derived tensors computed by projective models and End_D(A)(A[0]) = A

proof.text: For a bounded projective $P$, [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] says exactly that $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(P,E)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q(P),Q(E))$ is bijective for every $E$. With $E=P$, every derived endomorphism therefore has a chain representative unique up to homotopy; step 9 defines the required function on all of $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(Q(P))$. For another bounded projective representative $R$ and a derived isomorphism $w:Q(P)\to Q(R)$, the same bijection applied in both directions gives chain maps $f:P\to R$, $g:R\to P$ representing $w,w^{-1}$, with $gf\simeq1_P$ and $fg\simeq1_R$. If $v_R$ corresponds to $v_P$ under $w$, injectivity gives $v_R\simeq fv_Pg$. Then step 9 and degreewise cyclicity give $\operatorname{str}(v_R)=\operatorname{str}(fv_Pg)=\operatorname{str}(v_Pgf)=\operatorname{str}(v_P)$; the last equality uses $v_Pgf\simeq v_P$. In particular a quasi-isomorphism between the representatives gives precisely such a $w$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This supplies the missing implication from homotopy invariance to derived invariance.

source.place: Step 5, independence of the representative and passage from homotopy to derived morphisms

proof.text:
Finally verify the duality transport, so the preceding value agrees with the specified categorical trace, not just with some scalar function. For a chain map $f:P\to R$, its dual is $f^\vee(\varphi)=\varphi f$; it commutes with the displayed dual differentials. Frame expansion gives the two identities
$$(f\otimes1)\operatorname{coev}_P=(1\otimes f^\vee)\operatorname{coev}_R,\qquad \operatorname{ev}_R(1\otimes f)=\operatorname{ev}_P(f^\vee\otimes1).$$
For the first, both tensors are $\sum_{i,a,b} e^R_{i,b}\otimes\epsilon^P_{i,a}\,\epsilon^R_{i,b}(f(e^P_{i,a}))$; the second is equality after evaluation on $\varphi\otimes x$. Dualization preserves chain homotopy: if $f-f'=dh+hd$, the dual homotopy on a degree-$j$ functional is $\varphi\mapsto(-1)^j\varphi h$, indeed $d^\vee(t\varphi)=\varphi h d_P$ and $t(d^\vee\varphi)=\varphi d_R h$, because each coefficient is the product of two equal powers of $-1$. Their sum is precomposition by $d_Rh+hd_P$. Thus for the $f,g$ of step 11, $Q(f^\vee)$ and $Q(g^\vee)$ are inverse. Write $U=Q(P)$, $V=Q(R)$, $w=Q(f):U\to V$ and $z=Q(f^\vee):V^\vee\to U^\vee$. The two identities give
$$\operatorname{coev}_V=(w\otimes z^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_U,\qquad \operatorname{ev}_V=\operatorname{ev}_U(z\otimes w^{-1}).$$
For $v:U\to U$ and $v_V=wvw^{-1}$, naturality of the symmetry, verified in step 4, makes the transported trace composite
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ev}_V c_{V,V^\vee}(v_V\otimes1)\operatorname{coev}_V
&=\operatorname{ev}_U(z\otimes w^{-1})(z^{-1}\otimes w)c_{U,U^\vee}(v\otimes1)\operatorname{coev}_U\\
&=\operatorname{ev}_U c_{U,U^\vee}(v\otimes1)\operatorname{coev}_U.
\end{aligned}$$
Here $zz^{-1}=1$ and $w^{-1}w=1$ cancel the two tensor factors. The triangle composite on $V$ becomes $w[(1_U\otimes\operatorname{ev}_U)(\operatorname{coev}_U\otimes1_U)]w^{-1}=1_V$, since the intervening dual factors are $zz^{-1}=1$. The triangle on $V^\vee$ becomes $z^{-1}[(\operatorname{ev}_U\otimes1)(1\otimes\operatorname{coev}_U)]z=1_{V^\vee}$, since the intervening ordinary factors are $w^{-1}w=1$. Thus both the duality maps and the trace have the required transport formulas. For the finite-coefficient rings, [def-trf-categorical-trace] specifies these very frame maps, transport formulas and the unit-Hom bijection of step 10, so its trace coincides with ours. No finite-coefficient assumption was imposed in the general calculation.

source.place: Step 5 and unit proof, evaluation composite unchanged when duality is transported along an isomorphism
